key_insight: Rayleigh-Bénard convection preserves key circulation-statistics features known from homogeneous isotropic turbulence, especially away from the thermal boundary layer, but near-wall vortex structure is strongly reshaped by temperature coupling.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that small-scale circulation models and diagnostics developed for turbulence may transfer to buoyancy-driven flows, with special care required in thermal boundary layers near heated/cooled walls.
method: Direct numerical simulations of Rayleigh-Bénard convection at Ra = 10^9 and Pr ≈ O(1).
Analyze elementary vortices and their core aspect ratios within the thermal boundary layer.
Compute circulation PDFs for planar contours parallel to the walls and test the Area Rule.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that circulation PDFs in wall-parallel planes closely match HIT behavior and that the Area Rule remains well satisfied except possibly in a transitional region a few thermal boundary-layer thicknesses from the wall.
watch_item: Results are drawn from a specific high-Rayleigh-number, Prandtl-number-of-order-one regime, so the near-wall behavior and transitional-region findings may not generalize unchanged to other buoyancy or fluid-property conditions.
